title: Barks v. Silicon Foundation
summary: Twelve Warwood residents argue HB 2014 unconstitutionally strips local land-use and zoning control. AG J.B. McCuskey's office intervened to defend the statute, and on Oct 9 it cited this case in declining Berkeley County's request for a legal opinion. In late September the defendants moved to dismiss, arguing there is no ripe controversy. Judge David Sims denied the plaintiffs' request for discovery first and set Oct 28 for their response.

title: Tucker United, WVHC & Sierra Club v. DEP (Ridgeline air permit)
summary: On Aug 26 the Intermediate Court of Appeals dismissed both appeals on jurisdiction, not on the merits. Earlier, Judges Daniel Greear and Charles Lorensen recused over ties to Speaker Roger Hanshaw's firm Bowles Rice, and SCAWV refused Fundamental Data's bid to skip the ICA. Appalachian Mountain Advocates says the groups will refile.

next.t: Appeals refiled at the Supreme Court of Appeals

title: Mingo County residents v. TransGas, Army Corps, USFWS & FERC
summary: Judge Robert Chambers dismissed the TransGas claims in March and the agency claims on Jun 22, 2026. Attorney Stephen New (Beckley) plans new suits under EPCRA with adjacent residents and has named Penzance and QTS as future targets.

title: Possible county challenge to HB 2014
summary: Putnam Commission President Andy Skidmore says the county has talked with Monongalia County about suing over HB 2014. Monongalia Commissioner Sean Sikora says the law takes rights from counties. No suit has been filed. On Sep 29 the Putnam Commission instead adopted a resolution saying data center developers should fund 100 percent of water, sewer, and power upgrades. Skidmore said developers should follow county rules "as if House Bill 2014 didn't exist."

title: MARL 500 kV line (NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic)
summary: About 58.9 WV miles through Monongalia, Preston, Mineral, and Hampshire. On Aug 19 PSC Staff moved to make NextEra toll the case or have it dismissed. The Commission denied that on Sep 4, kept the Mar 6, 2027 decision date, and ordered NextEra to study using the existing Gore–Hampshire right-of-way instead. Staff witness Daniel Egnatoff recommended denial. The Jefferson County Commission, Hampshire, Mineral, and Harrison County Commissions, Friends of the Cheat, and the Hampshire County Farmland Protection Board weighed in. More than 2,000 protest signatures and letters were filed Aug–Nov. The evidentiary hearing ran five days, Oct 26–30, and ended a day early. It was live-streamed. Between Nov 2 and Nov 6 the docket added hearing transcripts and exhibits, two petitions to protest (199 and 72 signatures), 28 protest letters, three support letters, and one set of comments. Between Nov 9 and Nov 13 the docket added post-hearing exhibits filed by NextEra's counsel, a petition to protest with 513 signatures, four more protest letters, one support letter, and comments from the Hampshire County Commission's counsel, the Preston County Commission, and one individual. PSC Chair Charlotte Lane said at the close of testimony that the Commission would try to rule by the end of 2026; the statutory deadline is Mar 6, 2027. WBOY reports the Preston County Commission adopted a second resolution opposing the line Nov 9. Between Nov 18 and Nov 20 the docket added six briefs (three labeled initial briefs and three post-hearing briefs), two protest letters, and a petition to protest with 27 signatures.

title: Fort Martin 1,200 MW gas plant + 70 MW solar ($2.48B)
summary: Mon Power / Potomac Edison (FirstEnergy). Ten parties filed initial briefs on Aug 28: PSC Staff, the Consumer Advocate, WVEUG, the Sierra Club, Citizen Action Group / Solar United Neighbors / Energy Efficient WV, the WV Coal Association, Gas & Oil Association, WV Manufacturers Association, and the Building & Construction Trades Council. Reply briefs closed Sep 14. On Nov 17 the PSC approved the gas plant and three solar projects ($182M), with a customer surcharge the companies estimate starts at about $1.18 a month for residential customers. The companies must update the PSC on construction and costs starting January 2027. The PSC's Nov 17 notice describes a final order granting the certificate for the 1,200 MW combined cycle plant and 70 MW of solar, authorizing a surcharge, and closing the case. On Nov 19 WV News reported that the United Mine Workers of America and West Virginians for Energy Freedom criticized the approval, and that the final rate structure will be set in a later proceeding.

title: Appalachian Power / Wheeling Power large-load tariff
summary: Customers of 100 MW or more sign 12-year contracts and pay for at least 80% of contracted demand. ApCo says its contracted WV data-center load is "more than double" its 540 MW in Virginia.

title: PJM capacity market investigation: AEP's "FRR" status and Mon Power bidding
summary: Should Appalachian Power and Wheeling Power keep supplying their own capacity (Fixed Resource Requirement) instead of buying in PJM's auction, where data-center demand is pushing prices up? Mon Power responded Oct 22 and ApCo/WPCo Oct 30. Staff's recommendation is due 60 days later. Intervenors: the Consumer Advocate and WVEUG.

title: Mon Power / Potomac Edison Integrated Resource Plan
summary: On Aug 28 the Commission ordered the detailed data behind the IRP's summary tables and charts filed by Dec 1, 2026, with an updated plan due Dec 1, 2028.

title: HB 2014 generating-capacity rules: 69% coal capacity factor becomes "a goal, not a mandate"
summary: The PSC's general investigation into the rules HB 2014 requires for electric generating capacity. After taking public comment in September, the PSC filed revised rules in October, drawing partly on joint amendments from Appalachian Power and Mon Power. On Nov 10 the Legislature's Rule-Making Review Committee approved the rules, which keep the 69% coal capacity requirement as a goal rather than a mandate. The full Legislature is to review them in January.

title: Valley Link 765 kV: protests before the formal application
summary: On Sep 14, 2026 the PSC opened this file so residents can comment before Valley Link (Dominion / FirstEnergy / Transource) files for a certificate. It is not the official case. The real application will get its own number, expected late 2026 or early 2027, with a preferred route due early 2027. The Barbour, Upshur, Lewis, and Preston County Commissions oppose the line. PJM's latest update puts Valley Link at $5.1 billion, up from $2.9 billion in 2024, and moves in-service past 2029.

title: Monarch Cloud Campus LLC: 2.16 GW, 864 gas engines
summary: DEP's preliminary finding is that the plant meets requirements, and it is classed as a "major stationary source." The Oct 20 workshop was at Point Pleasant HS and the virtual hearing was Oct 29. Written comments were due before 5 p.m. Nov 13, 2026, and DEP's notice says only comments received by then, or given orally at the meetings, are considered before final action. DEP's notice lists no date for the final determination. Engineers: Joe Kessler and Edward Andrews.

sources.label: DEP: public comment and meetings, Monarch (notice dated 9/29/2026)

title: Monarch violations: sediment, flooding, dust
summary: Violation notices on May 24, May 28, Jun 4, and Jun 10; a July enforcement order after Jul 11 rain overwhelmed erosion controls; and an Aug 11 particulate-dust letter from DAQ Director Laura Crowder. Runoff flooded about six homes on May 23–24. Monarch reported corrective actions in an Aug 18 letter.

title: Buffalo campus: 288 diesel generators, 128 cooling towers
summary: Application received Jul 22, 2026 (DEP permit R13-3782, facility 079-00208). Projected 249 tons/yr of NOx. The Army Corps application shows 34+ acres of wetlands and 45,000+ feet of streams affected. As of Nov 18 the DEP lists no preliminary determination or comment deadline.

next.t: DEP preliminary determination and comment period (no date posted)

title: TransGas Adams Fork plants, Mingo County
summary: Two gas plants with 117 engines each to power data centers at Twisted Gun (Wharncliffe) and Harless Industrial Park (Holden).

title: Power Generation and Consumption Act
summary: Creates High Impact Data Center (≥90 MW) certification and microgrid districts of up to 2,250 acres, and preempts county and city zoning. Host counties get 30% of the property-tax revenue. Signed by Gov. Patrick Morrisey on Apr 30, 2025.

title: Certification rule + confidentiality
summary: Approves rule 145 CSR 20 and keeps certification petitions confidential. The House passed it 78-16. Local-control bills HB 5620 and SB 658, and the water-notice bill HB 5590, all died.

title: Responsible Data Center Development Plan
summary: Seven principles over 20 years, run by the Data Economy Office (Director Chris Morris). It promises a Data Center Advisory Council on setbacks and noise. No roster has been published.

title: Repeal or amend HB 2014
summary: Democratic Chair Mike Pushkin, Del. Shawn Fluharty, the WV NAACP (moratorium resolution), and the WVDCAP coalition are pushing local control, water protections, and a fairer county revenue share.
